newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded, diesel diffs steady.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded, diesel diffs steady.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot unleaded gasoline and diesel differentials were steady on Wednesday, leaving prices to track NYMEX futures, traders said.

Chicago basis remained stronger on an outage at Clark Refining and Marketing Co's 80,515 barrel per day Blue Island, Ill., refinery that affected an alkylation unit and fluid catalytic cracker, traders said.
The processing units went down on Tuesday and were expected back on line by Friday, traders said.
The American Petroleum Institute late Tuesday said gasoline stocks in primary storage at PADD II Midwest refineries rose a net 1.7 million barrels compared to the prior week.
The build was fueled by a continued blistering pace of production at Midwest refineries, which were operating at 97.4 percent of capacity on the week, the trade group said.
Low sulphur diesel stocks were up 758,000 barrels compared to the same week last year, while high sulphur diesel supplies were off 1.39 million barrels year-to-year.
Differentials on late-month deliveries remained weaker in both markets, prompting some activity in front-to-back trading.
Group Three early December low sulphur diesel differentials were bid 3.75 cents a gallon under the print, with later deliveries bid 4.0 cents a gallon under.
Chicago low sulphur diesel remained 1.25/1.0 cent a gallon under the print for prompt deliveries and 2.25/2.0 cent a gallon under the print for later deliveries.
High sulphur diesel was bid 4.50 cents a gallon under the print in Group Three and 1.75 cent a gallon under in Chicago.
